title: introduce-scanline-attn-kernel-with-rotary-alignment-and-pipelined-kv-prefetch
author: Nina Patel
body: Motivation: We hit a hard SLO regression for a set of long-dialog workloads where the existing fused Flash/rope paths performed poorly once per-request sequence variance exceeded our batching window. This PR introduces a new 'scanline' attention microkernel plus a lightweight rotary alignment pass and a pipelined KV prefetch stage. The goal is to reduce tail latency for skewed sequence distributions while preserving throughput on short sequences. High-level changes: 1) New CUDA kernel src/runtime/attn/scanline_kernel.cu implementing a memory-friendly scanline attention algorithm that walks KV tiles in patch order to improve L2 reuse for long prefixes. 2) Rotary alignment layer src/runtime/attn/rotary_align.cc which normalizes rotary offsets across heterogeneous model variants so fused ops can reuse precomputed trig lookup tables. 3) Pipelined KV prefetch orchestrator src/runtime/kv/prefetch_pipeline.cc that overlaps tensor DMA and kernel launches with the continuous-batcher, introducing an additional per-request prefetch hint and a global low-latency queue. 4) Scheduler hinting update src/runtime/scheduler/hints.h and runtime bindings to preferentially route high-variance sequence requests to the scanline kernel and warm KV cache proactively. 5) Small API surface addition in runtime config to allow ops teams to mark models as "rotary-aligned" for zero-cost compatibility. Performance: On our internal long-dialog benchmark (mean seq len 1024, 99th pct 4096) running on A100-40GB: - baseline: median 34ms, p99 312ms - with scanline + prefetch: median 29ms (-15%), p99 198ms (-36%) For short-sequence microbenchmarks (seq len <=128) we observe a median throughput change within +/-3%, no regressions in p95. Correctness and safety: The rotary_align pass is strictly idempotent and has guardrails to fallback to the existing rotary path if alignment metadata is missing. The new kernel has an optional debug-mode path that replays the old fused computation for bitwise comparison (disabled in release builds). Testing: added unit tests for alignment logic and prefetch pipeline, end-to-end integration tests in test/runtime/attn/test_scanline_end2end.py, and perf harness runs in perf/bench/scanline_campaign.yml. Rollout plan: merged behind a feature flag runtime.feature_scanline_attn; will enable on Canary pool for 48h, then incrementally enable for a subset of tenants with long-dialog traffic. Rollback is a single config flip. Related work: follows from ENG-4281 (continuous batching heuristics) and complements flashbridge experiments in ENG-4307. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the scanline kernel as an opt-in path; next PR will add autotuning to choose kernels per-model at deploy time.

Nina Patel: Added scheduler docs paragraph and appended batch-size microbenchmarks to the perf campaign (see scanline_campaign.yml).
Ariel Thompson: Please gate the debug verification path behind an env var; we don't want the replay enabled in release images.
Nina Patel: Moved replay verifier to DEBUG_VERIFY_SCANLINE env guard. Also added assertion to ensure fallback path when alignment metadata missing.
Samir Kaur: LGTM after small naming nit in prefetch_pipeline.cc; left a suggestion to rename PrefetchStage::dispatch -> enqueue_for_prefetch.

ci_checks: Perf bench: initially failed (outlier in short-seq microbench), rebased and tuned launch params, perf bench: pass
release_notes:
- Add 'scanline' attention kernel to reduce tail latency for long-dialog workloads.
- Rotary alignment pass for cross-variant fused-op reuse.
- Pipelined KV prefetch to overlap DMA with computation.
Rollout: feature gated, canary-first enable. No breaking changes expected.
